# Box2D.NET source provenance

- Upstream: https://github.com/ikpil/Box2D.NET
- Release tag: `3.1.654`
- Commit: `5efc96def866edbb4e5a9368d84de5bf8c2dcaca`
- Imported: all 233 C# files from `src/Box2D.NET/`, with the upstream MIT [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)
- Assembly: source is compiled into `Electron2D.dll`; no separate managed package is shipped

Local boundary and compiler adaptations:

1. Change 258 namespace-level `public` type/delegate declarations to `internal`; nested members remain in their upstream form. The resulting assembly export has zero Box2D.NET declarations.
2. Add `#nullable disable` to every imported file, matching the upstream project's nullability setting while keeping Electron2D-owned source strict.
3. Suppress the upstream-only XML comment diagnostics `CS1570` in `B2Delegates.cs` and `B2DynamicTrees.cs`, and `CS1587` in `B2MathFunction.cs`, `B2Contacts.cs`, `B2Ids.cs`, and `B2Solvers.cs`. Suppress the upstream constant-branch `CS0162` in `B2Solvers.cs`. These directives do not change runtime behavior.
4. Reuse a `B2StepContext` and graph-color block array per world, resetting transient fields on each step. Skip allocation of dummy overflow-contact state when there are no overflow contacts. These hot-path changes make the tested warmed contact, resting and moving body steps allocate zero managed bytes on the current Linux/.NET 8 path. The reusable-buffer portion is proposed to current upstream in [ikpil/Box2D.NET#101](https://github.com/ikpil/Box2D.NET/pull/101); the pinned release's overflow-contact methods no longer exist on upstream `main`.
5. Reuse the existing identity body state for static-body revolute warm-start and solve branches, which only read it. This removes 576 managed bytes per four-substep active pin frame in the checked Linux/.NET 10 path. The same change is proposed to current upstream in [ikpil/Box2D.NET#102](https://github.com/ikpil/Box2D.NET/pull/102).
6. Apply the same read-only identity-state reuse to static-body wheel warm-start and solve branches. The checked four-substep active groove path also drops from 576 to zero managed bytes per warmed frame. This companion change is included in [ikpil/Box2D.NET#102](https://github.com/ikpil/Box2D.NET/pull/102).

7. Preserve the removed reference instance in the spare slot during array swap-removal. New contact/island handles consume already constructed array slots. Sleeping solver-set buffers retain capacity across ordinary sleep/wake/destruction and release it only when the world is destroyed, including dormant cached slots. Runtime body/contact-cap preparation bounds the measured sandbox topology; denser or newly configured topology can still grow storage.
8. Extend wide contact arithmetic, indices, gather/scatter and layout checks to eight lanes using `Vector256<float>` storage so the JIT can retain vector locals. Skip the absent second normal/friction point only when all eight second-point normal masses are zero. Vector comparisons and conditional selection preserve the scalar NaN and signed-zero choices. Multiply/add remains separate. .NET supplies accelerated or portable fallback implementations. The single-worker stage executes its blocks directly; retained multiworker jobs preserve the existing graph-color barriers. A step-context worker-failure field lets a failed constraint job signal its peers instead of leaving the coordinator spinning. The field resets with the reusable context. The engine-owned scheduler is internal and does not replace the pinned solver. Lane checks, serial/parallel state hashes, native oracle and integration results are recorded in the [performance report](../../../docs/components/box2d-performance.md).

9. Arena growth preserves existing owned scratch objects and constructs only the new tail. Contact/joint pointer scratch arrays reserve empty reference slots, because these arrays gather existing graph objects before reading them. Runtime world preparation can reserve the retained arena before simulation demand grows.
10. AABB tree queries use an uninitialized 1,024-entry local traversal stack. Every live entry is assigned by a push before a pop reads it; capacity, traversal, filters and callbacks are unchanged. This removes whole-stack clearing from broad-phase and continuous-collision queries.

11. Solver task delegates are prepared together at type initialization, including infrequent island splitting and bullet work. First execution of those tasks no longer creates a delegate during a warmed step; scheduling and solver order are unchanged.

12. Polygon separation reads both polygon records by reference. The four-vertex support search evaluates independent coordinates in Vector128 lanes while retaining scalar reduction order and a scalar fallback. Separate multiply/add, edge tie selection, NaN and signed-zero behavior are checked against scalar arithmetic; maximum Smash state bytes match before/after the change.

13. An optional internal world callback replaces body integration stages during GPU-world development. The CPU path retains its existing stages. The integration-only numeric entry uses one worker; whole GPU solving runs on the owner while CPU collision stages retain workers. No backend callback is public. The GPU solve callback owns constraint preparation and publishes contact impulses directly to manifolds, plus prepared joint frames/coefficient state, before ordinary CPU finalization. CPU preparation/store tasks run only for the CPU path; per-frame CPU contact softness is also skipped when the GPU solver owns it. Typed arena abort and scheduler draining clear temporary step ownership after a failed GPU interval, allowing world disposal without replay.

14. An optional owner-thread manifold batch callback supplies computed geometry and feature-matched impulses to the common material/pre-solve/contact-transition path. The CPU path still computes its own manifolds when the callback is absent. Step reset and collision teardown clear the supplied array. A separate step-reset owner marker permits resident geometry lookup through contact graph updates; the GPU host consumes it once and also checks the generating context. Contact simulations preserve their signed source version and slot in CopyFrom (positive geometry batch, negative completed solver); stale or absent provenance uploads raw geometry instead. Contact creation and CPU manifold recomputation clear that version; other internal geometry replacements must do the same. Common center-of-mass shifts, feature pruning and pre-solve veto retain the source geometry contract. Generated manifolds now include GPU feature-matched normal/tangent/rolling impulses and persisted flags; b2UpdateContact retains anchor shifts and pre-solve veto but skips duplicate matching for this internal source. The GPU shader adapts the pinned circle/capsule/segment/polygon equations, retains MIT attribution and does not currently accept chain segments.

15. Retain virtual surface linear/angular velocity separately from integrated body state. Contact simulations copy both endpoints into scalar/SIMD/GPU constraints; query getters include the channel, while pose integration and actual kinematic travel exclude it. Body simulation clear/copy/type changes preserve/reset its lifecycle. Electron2D applies stored StaticBody and raw static state through the shared runtime helper and wakes contacts. Surface response, query snapshots, kinematic additivity and warmed allocation have CPU/GPU checks.

16. Scalar/SIMD contact constraints accumulate signed tangential impulse across warm starting and all solve substeps, alongside the existing normal sum. Manifold points publish both totals. Contact simulations record their native solve epoch through creation/copy/CPU store and GPU publication; sleeping retained manifolds cannot be mistaken for a new solve. Electron2D combines reported feature impulses across internal kinematic intervals and uses bounded depth-priority snapshots. GPU working records retain their layout by using reserved endpoint-vector fourth components for the two tangent totals.

17. An optional owner-thread broad-phase callback replaces only the tree-query task. The common move-result arena and user filter stay shared; ordered creation uses the separate optional callback described below. GPU traversal now performs self/moved/existing-pair, body/sensor, mask/group and joint filtering; an extracted shared helper invokes only the user callback and publishes the ordered pair. The shader implements the pinned table hash with split 32-bit arithmetic and walks the smaller joint list. Shape/joint filter metadata is sampled on CPU at binding or on dirty slots; unchanged records stay resident on GPU. Contact creation/destruction optionally notifies the GPU host of dirty contact IDs; its retained journal coalesces final keys for the GPU-owned lookup table. No observer is registered for CPU worlds. World reset and GPU disposal clear the observer. GPU traversal returns filtered candidates in CPU tree order and retries capacity overflow before publishing. Callback teardown/reset releases the GPU host reference. CPU worlds retain the original worker traversal when the callback is absent.

18. Optional dynamic-tree proxy notifications record shape IDs for creation, destruction, movement, enlargement and category edits. This boundary includes the direct bullet-enlargement lane; CPU worlds have no observer. GPU tree construction/refit uses its own resident hierarchy and receives only proxy deltas after binding/growth. CPU trees remain for shared queries/CCD and leaf publication ranks, so pair/callback order is preserved after independent GPU traversal. GPU disposal and tree reset detach observers. The category setter validates an allocated leaf instead of testing aliased child fields: those fields hold userData in a leaf. A focused Debug regression proves the old assertion failed for nonzero shape identity and the corrected guard permits the update.

19. Optional owner-thread shape/joint filter notifications cover shape creation after sensor initialization, destruction and filter edits, joint creation/destruction and collision-policy edits, and predecessor next-link changes during joint removal. The GPU host journals final slot values plus affected endpoint shape adjacency. Repeated edits/reuse coalesce before upload; disabled shapes remain represented. GPU scatter applies deltas and marks moved shapes from the query buffer with an epoch, avoiding full filter snapshots for ordinary movement. Binding, observer loss, capacity growth and epoch wrap force a full snapshot. CPU worlds register no observers; world reset and GPU disposal clear them.

20. Optional geometry notifications invalidate a GPU shape slot on creation/destruction and successful circle/capsule/segment/polygon edits, including type changes. A rejected degenerate capsule does not invalidate geometry. GPU geometry uploads are lazy at first overlapping contact use, coalesce repeated edits/references, and commit residency only after a validated fence. Movement and filter edits do not invalidate local geometry; material/hit-event invalidation is added by item 21. CPU worlds register no observer; world reset and GPU disposal detach it. Binding/observer changes and capacity growth clear cached residency.

21. A step-scoped completion marker lets the GPU collision callback publish complete contact updates and skip the CPU collision task, while retaining ordered contact bits, island/graph mutation and events. Native/default and Electron2D material mixing, touching/disjoint/start/stop/hit flags and mass-relative anchors execute in the GPU kernel. Retained workers publish ordinary contact mirrors and per-worker change bits; custom material and pre-solve callbacks execute on the owner after workers join. Worlds with custom material callbacks preserve serial publication order. The shared pre-solve helper preserves deepest-point arguments and veto semantics. Test-only speculative pruning now checks the second point's separation in its second branch, correcting a duplicated first-point condition; the GPU path matches it. Material and shape/body hit-event setters also invalidate resident shape inputs, including chain material updates. Reset and collision cleanup clear the completion marker.

22. An optional broad-phase creation callback consumes the ordered, user-filtered pair lists. GPU prefix allocation owns contact IDs, unsigned generation increments and initial shape/body/set/event/material records. The shared native creation core imports validated prepared identities and publishes body adjacency, contact simulation and pair-table links; custom material callbacks retain their original order and position. The native ID pool has an optional ordered allocation/free observer and a checked claim operation for GPU-chosen IDs. The GPU pool snapshots at binding/growth/observer loss, applies ordinary frees in parallel and replays rare mixed external mutations serially. Contact simulations retain their generation through graph copies, avoiding a random contact-object lookup during pair packing. GPU collisions consume resident identity slots by integer ID/generation; shape/pair headers no longer encode IDs as floats. CPU worlds leave both callbacks unset and keep original allocation/creation. World reset clears them; GPU disposal detaches only owned callbacks. Injected failure after creation verifies the existing failed-world/no-replay boundary.

23. Prepared contact creation now imports GPU-computed next links and insertion-time counts while publishing the same ordered body adjacency prefix. Custom material callbacks observe the original intermediate state. An optional link observer runs after CPU insertion/removal and journals the changed contact, both bodies and neighboring edges. GPU-owned publication suppresses its own journal entries; external CPU changes coalesce to final records. GPU endpoint sorting and segmented construction retain final links/head/counts in 16-byte records, with a separate head commit pass. Observer loss, world changes and capacity growth restore snapshots. World reset clears the observer and host disposal detaches only owned callbacks. Tests read back all retained GPU links and compare them with the mirror, including body reuse, disable/enable/type edits and custom callback-visible topology. CPU removal, island/graph mutation and mirror publication remain shared.

24. Complete GPU collision updates can supply prepared disjoint-contact removals. The state-change loop retains its ascending contact-ID order, importing each GPU previous/next/head/count prefix into the common removal core at its original position among started/stopped contacts. Events, pair-table mirror updates, graph/island removal and wake behavior remain shared. A finish callback verifies full batch consumption and pool counts. The GPU unlinks independent body lists in parallel, executes each body's removals in order, invalidates resident slots and appends free IDs; own free/link notifications are suppressed. External CPU authoring removals keep their original path and journals. The numeric manifold-only callback does not select GPU removal. World reset clears both callbacks and all existing integration/solve/manifold callbacks; the latter three previously survived raw world reuse and could call a disposed GPU host. Reset also clears the retained step context, releasing its body-array and GPU-owner references. Host teardown preserves another owner's callbacks. Focused tests compare full GPU adjacency, graph slots, ordered free IDs, begin/end events and callback-visible lists through churn; an injected mid-publication failure verifies no replay and disposal.

25. An optional splitIsland callback replaces DFS discovery/list construction for dirty awake islands. The GPU finds connected components from ordered contact/joint adjacency, then emits the original per-component DFS lists. The host validates and reserves all mirror allocations before publication, allocates island IDs in seed order, imports membership/lists and frees the base ID last. CPU worlds retain the original splitter. Scheduled GPU splitting runs on the owner instead of enqueueing compute work on a solver worker; explicit body sleep reaches the same callback. Reset clears it, and GPU disposal/rebinding preserves another owner's callback. Island merges, graph coloring, sleep decisions and solver-set transfer remain shared CPU stages. Conformance compares full list and ID-pool order, static/disabled/non-touching edges, cycles, sleep/wake, four-worker scheduling and warmed allocation.

26. Optional begin/change/finish island callbacks bracket the ordered contact-state loop. GPU weighted union, list concatenation and contact insertion/removal plan the complete final graph; a parallel member pass resolves merge parents. The original loop preserves CPU wake/set-transfer order and frees prepared island IDs at their original positions, while final membership/list publication precedes validation. Immediate authoring graph edits and ordinary CPU worlds retain their original path. No user callback runs inside the incomplete mirror interval. The host validates complete results before publication, and failed-space teardown releases raw storage in bulk instead of traversing a partially published graph. Reset clears all three hooks. The initial GPU storage used full graph snapshots; patch 27 replaces those transfers. Ordered union is still serial and its measured cost remains documented.

27. A serialized islandGraphChanged observer journals graph records by kind and slot. Body/contact/joint creation and destruction, list neighbors, authoring merges/unlinks and CPU/GPU split publication all participate; repeated changes coalesce until the next nonempty contact batch. Final values are sampled after the authoring operation. Prepared GPU island destruction suppresses its own duplicate journal entry, but contact lifecycle changes still journal slot identity. The native island-pool identity, observer ownership and graph-buffer capacity determine snapshot invalidation. GPU dirty-slot compaction returns only changed lists/members; output overflow regathers completed state without replaying graph mutations. Reset clears the observer. The original CPU graph remains unchanged when no observer/backend is installed.

28. GPU contact-list maintenance now builds an ordered concatenation tree during weighted union and resolves list boundaries/removal runs in parallel. Winner/free-ID order and final native lists remain unchanged; removal records may reference the final surviving root because native removal only consumes their membership transition. Body/joint concatenation and weighted union are still serial. The existing native begin/change/finish integration and journal hooks are unchanged. Full graph validation precedes publication, and malformed GPU graph input is covered by the error-gate test.

29. Optional begin/select/finish constraint-color callbacks bracket the contact-state loop. The GPU batch predicts ordered touching-contact changes and collision-triggered sleeping-set wakes, assigning colors to the waking contacts/joints before the triggering contact. Shared contact/joint insertion consumes prepared colors and updates ordinary body bitsets instead of searching on CPU; removal consumes the corresponding prepared operation before its unchanged swap-removal. Without an active batch, both use the original CPU greedy assignment, now shared to remove duplicated contact logic. World reset clears all callbacks. The GPU host validates color bounds, occupancy and publication identity/generation/order; partial failure has no CPU replay. Full bitset snapshots and serial GPU assignment remain measured limits; authoring coloring and solver-set transfer remain on CPU.

The library remains an internal backend. Electron2D public signatures use only Electron2D-owned types. Review every upstream update against this pinned version, license, internalization and integration tests before replacing these files.
